This is a small, self-contained Python script designed to generate plausible names. It's a stepping stone for building a name-predicting model, not a mature software system.

Bigram_counts.py is the foundation — it builds a 27×27 matrix of character transition frequencies from a training text file called `names.txt`. The two dependent files use this data: nn_bigram.py trains a neural net with gradient descent to learn the same matrix, while sampling.py converts the matrix into probability distributions and randomly walks through character space to generate new names. If bigram_counts.py returns an unexpected shape or counts, both downstream modules that depend on it could break. There are no database, queue, or network dependencies in this project.
